og.title: Center on Pervasive Personalized Intelligence (PPI)
og.description: The Internet of Things (IoT) marks the dawn of a technological revolution that rivals the industrial revolution. In this new era, intelligent computing becomes anticipatory, proactive, and adaptive. The next big growth in IoT systems will come from pushing Pervasive Personalized Intelligence (PPI) to the edge of the network, where latency is critical, and mobility, privacy, and context awareness are essential qualities of the application.The goal of the Center for Pervasive Personalized Intelligence (PPI) is to enable the next generation of IoT systems to be more proactive and personalized without compromising security and privacy, thereby improving decision-making, increasing efficiency and enabling new types of computing applications. The PPI Center will support the thrusts that enable an entirely new class of applications with intelligence that is predictive instead of reactive, thus making processes more efficient and saving time, energy, and money.Operationalizing compute-intensive AI applications to run on the edge, where compute resources are constrained, is a fundamental technical challenge. Moreover, their complexity will also pose new challenges for security, governance, programmability, and usability. The multi-university, multi-industry PPI Center can address these formidable challenges with a broader solution strategy. The PPI Center works alongside industry members: (i) as a research and development partner to help them build a platform on which they can build smart applications for various verticals, and (ii) as a center of excellence to create and disseminate a systematic body of knowledge required for building PPI applications.

checks.label: HTTPS (required for service workers)
checks.why: HTTPS is required for service workers and most install prompts.

checks.label: Web app manifest declared
checks.why: A web app manifest is required for installability and controls how the app appears when launched.

checks.label: Service worker registered
checks.why: A service worker is what makes offline access, caching, and background sync possible.

checks.label: Theme color declared
checks.why: Theme color controls the browser chrome/status-bar color when the site is installed or bookmarked.

checks.label: Apple touch icon (iOS/bookmark icon)
checks.why: iOS uses this icon for home-screen bookmarks and "Add to Home Screen" — without it the icon falls back to a screenshot.

checks.label: Manifest fetched and parsed successfully
checks.why: A manifest that fails to parse cannot drive installability or launch behavior even if the link is present.

checks.label: Manifest declares a maskable icon
checks.why: A maskable icon lets the OS safely crop/mask the app icon on different device shapes without clipping content.

checks.label: Service worker is active (not just registered)
checks.why: An active service worker (not just registered) is what actually intercepts requests and serves cached content.

checks.label: Service worker controls this page load
checks.why: A controlling service worker means THIS page load is being served/intercepted, not just a future one.

checks.label: Meets basic installability criteria
checks.evidence: no readable web app manifest; no service worker registered
checks.why: Determines whether the browser can realistically offer "Add to Home Screen" / install, based on manifest + service worker + HTTPS together.
